@hariharanr@ami.com - Thanks for this documentation. This was a well needed one.
I think this document is best fit as obmc-ikvm/README.md rather than in openbmc/docs since this does not talk about the design aspect rather talks about how to interact with a repository/daemon.

I’ve added a document that explains how to view or access the KVM — more like a usage guide. For technical details like kernel configuration, device tree, and other changes, I’m planning to add a separate section in the obmc-ikvm README. Does that sound good to you?

yes, sure  - a new enablement patch sounds good as well.

I still think obmc-ikvm/README.md is the best fit for this document. If at all may be we can have a symlink to obmc-ikvm/README.md here. But would let docs maintainer decide what's the best way forward. From the content perspective I am okay with the document.
I will create a new PR for updating obmc-ikvm/README.md

have you created this?

if not why is it marked resolved.

id so a link is appreciated.

I haven’t created the PR yet, as I’m still figuring out what needs to be captured. I need to review the code and gather the relevant details before proceeding. I also haven’t seen any activity in the obmc-ikvm repository so far, so I feel it might be more appropriate to document this here. Let me know your thoughts.
I think its also a good idea to capture the details on what needs to be added in the BMC device tree for this to work - for example the `human interface device` & the `video device` related details.
I’ll create a separate pull request for the obmc-ikvm repository to add this.
Its also a good idea to also document if the `host kernel` needs to have some sort of kernel option enabled to push the pixel frames to BMC.
I’ll create a separate pull request for the obmc-ikvm repository to add this.
can you also add a pointer on the limitation of external clients not being able to connect with <bmcip>:<port> directly & rather why we had to create an SSH tunnel ?

Typically, in production firmware, ssh port forwarding might be disabled due to security concerns. A small note can be added to highlight that, SSH server needs to be configured with local port forwarding option enabled for this access method to work.

In dropbear case it should be running without '-j' option.
https://linux.die.net/man/8/dropbear

Can be updated like below for better readability

ssh -L <localport>:localhost:<bmc-kvm-port> <bmc-user>@<bmc-hostname>

where,
localport    - Port number used for VNC client to connect (e.g., 1234)
bmc-kvm-port - Port number used by for KVM service in BMC firmware (default 5900)
bmc-user     - BMC firmware SSH username
bmc-hostname - BMC hostname / IP address for SSH access

e.g., `ssh -L 1234:localhost:5900 root@192.168.1.1`

I think it's a possibility.   I might be convinced that how to access it is a system integration issue beyond the iKVM repository scope.   I'd like to see a draft showing it's too much for there before addinf here.

this typo is in me.  `use guide` should read `user guide`

My goal was to add a document to help users how to launch and access KVM, since there’s currently no document for that. But based on the feedback, it looks like the scope is growing beyond just launching KVM.
For now, I think it’s okay to include just the basic steps to launch KVM. If we want to add more details (like how to enable KVM or handle system-level integration) it might need more time and discussion. Let me know your thoughts.

This directory is called design and it's supposed to discuss the motivation and thoughts on creating the function.

better but it still reads as secure until completing the long sentence which qualifies it.  A suggestion to build upon:

The host Video is directly connected to the BMC, along with a emulated USB keyboard and mouse.  These devices can be controlled remotely by using a secure tunnel to proxy the VNC protocol.   The VNC protocol itself is not secure.

The web server provides a secure websocket (was) tunnel.   Alternatively a ssh session to the BMC can be used to provide a secure tunnel to your local system.
